turns.assistant_text:
Here are some notable AI news highlights from today:

1. **[Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions](https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/client-alerts/20261110-agentic-ai-raises-new-questions-for-financial-institutions)** - This article discusses how AI is evolving from merely answering questions to acting on behalf of users, raising important issues regarding identity, authentication, and authority in financial transactions.

2. **[Stanford's Century-Long AI Study Admits It's Already Out of Date](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/11/10/stanfords-century-long-ai-study-admits-its-already-out-of-date/5308574)** - A report highlights the transformative impact of AI on science and research, noting the urgency of understanding how AI affects collective cognition and moral behavior, especially in light of recent academic retractions.

3. **[IBM and Microsoft Announce a New AI Agent Platform Designed for Industry-Specific Transformation](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2026/11/10/ibm-and-microsoft-announce-a-new-ai-agent-platform-designed-for-industry-specific-transformation)** - This announcement reveals a collaboration aimed at integrating AI into business processes, emphasizing the need for organizations to leverage AI for competitive advantage.

4. **[Fall Staff Town Hall Highlights ‘Human-Centered AI’ at Notre Dame](https://ndworks.nd.edu/news/fall-staff-town-hall-highlights-human-centered-ai-community-partnerships)** - The University of Notre Dame discusses its initiatives to use AI in research while maintaining a focus on human-centered approaches and ethical considerations.

5. **[Using AI to Screen Existing Compounds for Therapeutic Potential](https://www.pittwire.pitt.edu/features-articles/2026/11/10/drug-screening-generative-ai)** - Researchers at the University of Pittsburgh are utilizing generative AI to identify existing compounds that could have therapeutic applications, streamlining the drug discovery process.

These articles reflect the ongoing developments and discussions surrounding AI across various sectors.

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: Stanford's century-long AI study admits it's already out of date
items.summary:
Science, the report says, is being transformed by AI as it accelerates research timelines and opens up novel challenges. At the same time, the report cautions that "we will need to understand how AI-mediated information environments reshape collective cognition and moral behavior." The recent retraction of some 1,400 scholarly papers for failure to meet academic standards highlights the urgency of that message. [...] It identifies scaling as the engine of AI's advance, but also points to the growing cost and difficulty of obtaining training data as constraints on further progress.

The report likens AI's disruptive potential to that of the World Wide Web – without dwelling on the irony that the web itself is among the things being disrupted. It points to creative industries, computer programming, and mathematics as fields once deemed beyond the reach of automation that are now being upended. [...] "The report was written by humans, and its authors used AI primarily to transcribe and summarize meetings, support dictation, and check drafts for typos, consistency, duplication, tone, and structure. In some cases, AI suggested rewording of human-written text. AI was also used to compare this report with previous AI100 reports, identifying where expectations and reality have diverged or converged over five years. items.title: IBM and Microsoft announce a new AI agent platform designed for industry-specific transformation - Source
items.summary: “Clients are no longer looking for AI that simply helps people do the same work a little faster. They want to build an agentic business,” said Mohamad Ali, Senior Vice President and Head of IBM Consulting. “Microsoft and IBM are helping organizations bring human expertise and digital labor together in a way that can scale across the enterprise, to turn AI from a productivity aid into a real competitive advantage.” [...] “AI is evolving quickly, and our focus at SEI is on applying it with intention in ways that strengthen trust, enhance human decision-making and create meaningful value across our business,” said Sneha Shah, Chief AI Strategist and Head of SEI Next. “Our work with IBM Consulting and Microsoft is helping us explore how emerging capabilities could support critical processes and be responsibly scaled over time, with the goal to create better experiences for our employees and clients. By combining [...] “Enterprise AI will be won by organizations that can turn their data, industry expertise and AI into action,” said Rodrigo Kede Lima, President, Microsoft Frontier Company. “Together, Microsoft and IBM Consulting are bringing the best of our technology and expertise, to help customers move from AI ambition to business impact faster and with confidence.”

items.title: Fall Staff Town Hall highlights ‘human-centered AI,’ community partnerships | Latest | NDWorks | University of Notre Dame
items.summary:
McGreevy highlighted Notre Dame's opportunities to use AI to advance research, particularly through the Data, AI, and Computing Initiative, led by Nitesh Chawla, the Frank M. Freimann Professor of Computer Science and Engineering and Lucy Family Director for AI & Academic Strategy, as well as the University’s growing strength in AI ethics, including the work of Meghan Sullivan, the Wilsey Family College Professor of Philosophy and founding director of the Institute for Ethics and the Common [...] From the staff perspective, Cullinan said AI presents opportunities to work more efficiently and better steward the University's resources. But those efforts would remain “human-centered," a dynamic he said might seem contradictory at other universities.

“Not at Notre Dame,” Cullinan said. “I think the most important asset that we have, and will have, is our people.” [...] “What will set our students apart is their competency in interpersonal skills: their ability to make moral judgments, to recognize injustice, and to work on addressing that," he said.

McGreevy echoed Father Dowd's characterization of a "bilingual" education, saying students should still be challenged even as AI makes some assignments easier.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: People should always be in control of the future.
items.summary:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.
